question: 18-year-old boy with breast pain and retroareolar nodule on palpation. What is the most frequent cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> hormonal changes during puberty -> breast tissue growth in males -> 80% CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> common in adolescent boys -> benign condition -> 75% CHAIN: Pubertal gynecomastia -> typically resolves on its own -> self-limiting condition -> 80%
enhanced_information: Pubertal gynecomastia is the most frequent cause of breast pain and retroareolar nodule in an 18-year-old boy. It is a benign condition commonly seen in adolescent boys, typically resolving on its own due to hormonal changes during puberty. Evidence supports the link between adolescent gynecomastia and breast tissue hypertrophy as a manifestation of puberty.
analysis: Based on standard medical knowledge, the most frequent cause of breast pain and retroareolar nodule in an 18-year-old boy is likely to be pubertal gynecomastia. This condition is common during puberty due to hormonal changes.
